author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Actor and UMass Amherst alumnus Richard Gere is returning to the university for a special screening of a documentary created with the Dalai Lama, according to Western Mass News.

The campus appearance reconnects Gere with the university he attended before beginning a career spanning stage and film. He has also spent decades supporting humanitarian causes and advocating for Tibetan rights, making the documentary project closely connected to his public work beyond acting.

The film centers on the Dalai Lama’s reflections about compassion, inner peace and the pressures facing people in the modern world. Gere was involved with the project behind the scenes, and the Amherst screening gives students and the wider community an opportunity to hear about that collaboration in a university setting.

Western Mass News announced the event Wednesday but did not include ticketing or access details in its brief web report. Prospective attendees should confirm the schedule and admission information through UMass Amherst before traveling. The visit is notable both as a cultural event and as a homecoming for one of the university’s best-known former students.
dek: The actor and university alumnus is returning to campus for a special presentation of a documentary made in collaboration with the Dalai Lama.
headline: Richard Gere returns to UMass Amherst for Dalai Lama documentary screening
